stil: Vertical 9:16 key frame for an animated historical short film set in France in the 1830s. Painterly cinematic illustration, high-end animated feature concept art, rich chiaroscuro lighting, consistent with the attached character sheets (François Blanc: navy tailcoat, cream cravat, black top hat; his identical twin Louis Blanc: burgundy tailcoat, grey waistcoat, black cravat, grey top hat, brass-knob cane). Historically accurate 1830s details: no gas lamps (oil lanterns only), no paper money (gold and silver franc coins), Notre-Dame WITHOUT its central spire. Keep the top 22% of the frame calm and uncluttered for on-screen titles. No text, no letters, no watermark.

sahneler.vo: 1834. Bir telgraf memuru, devletin mesajına kasten bir hata ekliyor.

sahneler.prompt: Night in Tours, 1834. Low angle close shot of the Chappe telegraph mechanism on the roof of a small stone station: the regulator beam and its two indicator arms crisply silhouetted against a huge full moon partly veiled by thin drifting clouds, a cold blue rim light on the wood; in the foreground the hand of the telegraph operator (grey wool uniform sleeve) grips the iron control lever, lit by a warm oil lantern; a faint shooting star streaks across the sky. Rooftops of a small provincial town below, no famous monuments. Deep blue palette with one warm amber accent. The Chappe optical telegraph MUST look like this (see the attached silhouette reference): a single straight wooden mast rising from the roof of a small stone station hut; at the top of the mast, one long horizontal wooden beam (the regulator) pivoting at its center; at each end of that beam, a shorter wooden arm (indicator) hinged so it can point up or down — overall like a big letter T with bent ends. It is NOT a windmill, has NO blades, NO sails, NO metal lattice.

Long shadows toward the camera, blue moonlight rim light, amber lantern fill.
